Read WEIGHTS_LICENSE.md on the LoRA's page before downloading. Keep the credit: 80s Horror LoRA by Sam Wasserman (wassermanproductions.com). Powered by MiniMax H3.
notes: The look of a 1970s-80s horror movie: VHS for neon, tape and 80s video, or 16mm film for warm grindhouse grain. Write the light and the place, what happens, the camera and the sound; the trigger word brings the era. Made for 1280x704 or 1344x768, 5 to 8 seconds, 20 steps.
what: The look of a 1970s-80s horror movie: VHS or 16mm film.

name: Camera Motion
author: Jojocodex
licence: The author publishes this file under Apache-2.0. It was trained on MiniMax H3, whose Community License Agreement (territory limits, Acceptable Use Policy) still governs the base model you run it on.
what: Camera moves the base model tends to miss: push-in, pull-back, orbit, tracking, aerial, crane, pan, macro.
notes: Write the prompt as: subject, place, the camera move, light and style. Name the move in plain words, for example 'slow push-in with subtle lateral tracking' or 'slow pull-back combined with a gentle orbit'. 0.8 is gentle, 1.0 is definite, above 1.2 the picture can turn unstable. The author's page has a library of 55 prompts.

name: Head-mounted FPV
author: neph1
licence: The weights are a Model Derivative of MiniMax H3 under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement, with its territory limits, commercial terms and Acceptable Use Policy. Read the licence on the LoRA's page before downloading.
what: A first-person view from a camera on the head, with the bob of walking or running.
notes: The author's page gives no trigger word or settings (it mirrors a Civitai upload). Describe the shot as seen through the person's own eyes: 'first-person view from a head-mounted camera, hands visible, the view bobs with each step'.

name: Equirectangular 360°
author: shamanic

styles.360° layout: Equirectangular 360-degree panoramic video: the frame is a full spherical projection, a complete environment wrapping around the viewer on all sides, with the horizon at the vertical middle of the frame.

licence: The weights are a Model Derivative of MiniMax H3 under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement, with its territory limits, commercial terms and Acceptable Use Policy. Read the licence on the LoRA's page before downloading.
what: A full-sphere 360° panorama video with sound, for VR players.
notes: Made for a 21:9 frame: pick Custom size, 1120x480. The whole frame is the sphere: resize the clip to 2:1 and add 360 metadata for a VR player. Describe the place, the motion and the sound; a still camera works best. Seams at the wrap and stretching at the poles can still happen.

name: 360° Orbit
author: pablodawson
licence: The weights are a Model Derivative of MiniMax H3 under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement, with its territory limits, commercial terms and Acceptable Use Policy. Read the licence on the LoRA's page before downloading.
what: One photo becomes a frozen-moment 360° orbit that ends on the frame it started from.
why: It needs the same picture as the first and the last frame of the clip. The Studio sets a first frame only, so this LoRA cannot do its orbit here yet.
notes: Author's settings: 768x768, 73 frames, 28 passes, strength 1.0, no sound, and the author's fixed prompt.

name: Transformation
author: Ashmotv
licence: The weights are a Model Derivative of MiniMax H3 under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement, with its territory limits, commercial terms and Acceptable Use Policy. Read the licence on the LoRA's page before downloading.
what: Morphs one picture into another, element by element.
why: It needs two pictures: the start frame and the target frame of the clip. The Studio sets a first frame only, and its LoRA hub does not reach reference clips yet.
notes: Author's prompt: '[Shot 1] Picture 1 Tr@nsf0rmation into Picture 2 with individual elements and subjects Tr@nsf0rmation into one another.'

name: Turnaround
author: matlod
licence: The weights are a Model Derivative of MiniMax H3 under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement, with its territory limits, commercial terms and Acceptable Use Policy. Read the licence on the LoRA's page before downloading.
what: A five-view character sheet (front to back) from one reference picture.
why: It makes still pictures, not a clip, through the author's own five-view sampler for ai-toolkit. The Studio has no such sampler.
notes: Strength 1.0 for rotation, about 0.7 for likeness, on the Ref2VA model.

name: Keyframe Animation
author: alvdansen
licence: The author's own H3 Keyframe Animation Adapter License 1.0.0, on top of the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement. The files are gated: you accept the terms on the author's page with your own Hugging Face account.
what: Hand-drawn animation on held frames: the next key drawing, an inbetween, or a short held sequence from one or two drawings.
why: The files are gated on the author's page (you accept the author's licence there), each is 1.9 GB, and they work from reference drawings. The Studio's LoRA hub does not reach reference clips yet.
notes: Three adapters: hero (1 drawing), tween (2 drawings), sequence (2 drawings).

name: Character Swap
author: Akatz Labs (akatz-ai)
licence: The weights are a Model Derivative of MiniMax H3 under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement, with its territory limits, commercial terms and Acceptable Use Policy. Read the licence on the LoRA's page before downloading.
what: Replaces a person in a source clip with the person in a reference picture, keeping the scene.
why: It works on reference clips (a source video and a picture of the new person). The Studio's LoRA hub does not reach reference clips yet. Without it, 'A picture and a video' in the create wizard already swaps a person.
notes: Strength 1.0, no trigger: name the person to replace in the prompt. Shots of 4 to 5 seconds worked best for the author.

name: Person Remover
author: Akatz Labs (akatz-ai)
licence: The weights are a Model Derivative of MiniMax H3 under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement, with its territory limits, commercial terms and Acceptable Use Policy. Read the licence on the LoRA's page before downloading.
what: Removes a chosen person from a video and rebuilds the background.
why: It runs inside the author's ComfyUI workflow, which tracks the person with SAM 3.1, paints a green mask and needs a clean first frame. The Studio has no mask step.

name: Natural Face Speech
author: vpakarinen
licence: The author publishes this file under Apache-2.0. It was trained on MiniMax H3, whose Community License Agreement (territory limits, Acceptable Use Policy) still governs the base model you run it on.
what: More natural face muscles and clearer English speech for a person talking to the camera.
notes: Text to video or from a first frame. Author's prompt shape: 'she is speaking into a mic, she maintains eye contact with the viewer saying: ...'. Made for 720x1280 at 20 to 30 passes.

name: Motion Continuity Repair
author: JOKER141
licence: The author states no licence for this file. It was trained on MiniMax H3, whose Community License Agreement applies to the base model and to derivatives of it. Ask the author before any use beyond your own.
what: Keeps fast movement connected: fewer broken transitions, less unwanted slow motion, closer to the prompt.
notes: For running, sport, dance, tumbling, fights. About 0.9 alone; 0.5 to 0.7 beside Combat Base V2. Too high can rebuild the whole movement or change the sound. The trigger word is optional.

name: Combat Base V2
author: JOKER141
licence: The author states no licence for this file. It was trained on MiniMax H3, whose Community License Agreement applies to the base model and to derivatives of it. Ask the author before any use beyond your own.
what: Faster, harder-hitting fight movement, and livelier body movement and sound in dialogue scenes.
notes: The prompt still decides what the fighters do; the LoRA changes how it is performed. Write the action first, then any dialogue. The author gives no strength figure.

name: Weapon Combat
author: JOKER141
licence: The author states no licence for this file. It was trained on MiniMax H3, whose Community License Agreement applies to the base model and to derivatives of it. Ask the author before any use beyond your own.
what: Sword, staff and other weapon fights that hold together better.
notes: Use it alone: stacked with Combat Base V2 or Motion Continuity Repair it can turn unstable. The author says its training includes finishing moves and dismemberment, so it can produce graphic violence if the prompt asks for a kill.

name: Spatial Physics

notes: The author calls it a test release and suggests 0.3 to 0.5: a light push toward real physics on top of the base model.
